docs.title: vexy-formi
docs.text:
vexy-formi formats and minifies source files by handing each file to an external tool that is already installed on your machine: ruff or black for Python, biome, prettier or dprint for JavaScript and CSS, esbuild or swc to minify JavaScript, and so on. It finds the files, picks a tool per file type, runs the tools in parallel and reports what happened.

The package installs one command, vfor, and a Python package, vexy_formi.

docs.title: What goes in, what comes out
docs.text:
You give vfor a directory or a file and an operation:

  • vfor fmt <path> formats every supported file in place.
  • vfor mini <path> minifies every supported file in place.

For each file the tool:

  1. Skips it if it matches an exclusion pattern, is empty, larger than 100 MB, binary, unreadable or not writable.
  2. Looks up the file's extension in a fixed list of tools for that operation, for example .py → ruff, then black.
  3. Runs the first tool that is installed. If that tool fails, it tries the next one.
  4. Records the size before and after.

At the end it prints a summary such as Processed 4 files. With --verbose it lists each file.

vfor fmt src/ --verbose

Successful files:
  test.json (0.116s)
  test.js (0.122s)
  test.css (0.024s)
  test.py (0.149s)

docs.title: What it is not
docs.text:
• It is not a formatter itself. Without the external tools it does nothing. vfor tools shows which are installed; vfor install tries to install them.
  • It does not read each tool's settings for you. A tool such as dprint still needs its own dprint.json.
  • It is not reversible. The files are rewritten in place; see Safety and backups before you run it on work you have not committed.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text: If you want to… Read Install vfor and the tools it calls Installation Format a project for the first time Quick start Look up a command or flag CLI reference See which tool handles which file type Tools and file types Change worker count or exclusion patterns Configuration Understand what is skipped, what is asked, what is backed up Safety and backups Call it from Python Python API Fix a problem Troubleshooting Work on the code Development

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: vfor is built with Python Fire from the VFor class in src/vexy_formi/cli.py. Run vfor with no command to list the commands.

docs.title: How arguments work
docs.text:
• A positional argument can also be given by name: vfor fmt src/ and vfor fmt --path=src/ are the same.
  • Boolean flags switch on by name (--verbose) and off with a no prefix (--nobackup, --norecursive).
  • Flag names use underscores: --dry_run, --create_baseline.
  • Most flags also have a one-letter form, shown below.
  • List values are written as Python-style lists: --exclude='["*.min.js", "vendor/**"]'.

  • To see a command's flags without running it, put -- before --help:

    vfor mini -- --help

docs.title: fmt
docs.text:
Format files in place.

vfor fmt                    # current directory, recursively
vfor fmt src/
vfor fmt app.py
vfor fmt src/ --norecursive # top level of src/ only
vfor fmt src/ --dry_run --verbose
Flag Short Default Meaning --path -p . File or directory to process --recursive -r on Descend into subdirectories --exclude -e none Extra exclusion patterns, as a list --verbose -v off Print each file and a per-file result list --backup -b on Intended to keep a backup of each file; see the note below --dry_run -d off Find files and pick tools, but run nothing --force -f off Skip the confirmation for large runs

--backup has no effect in this version

The flag is passed along, but the code path that runs the tools does not write backup files. See Safety and backups.

The extensions fmt handles are listed in Tools and file types.

docs.title: mini
docs.text:
Minify files in place. Same flags as fmt.

vfor mini dist-src/
vfor mini site/ --exclude='["*.min.*"]' --verbose

The extensions mini handles are listed in Tools and file types. Files whose type has no minifier, such as .py, are not picked up when you give a directory; a single file of such a type fails with No minification tool available for .py.

docs.title: Output of fmt and mini
docs.text:
While running, a progress bar shows the counts of successful and failed files, the size saved and the rate in files per second. At the end:

  • Failed: <n> files, if any failed.
  • Processed <n> files, followed for mini by the total size change, for example +6.0% size. With --verbose the elapsed time follows; with --dry_run, (preview).
  • With --verbose, a Failed files: list with each error, and a Successful files: list. For mini each line shows original → final bytes, ±percent; for fmt it shows the time taken.

A positive percentage means the file got smaller.

docs.title: tools
docs.text:
vfor tools

Show the 13 tools vfor knows about, whether each is installed, its type (minifier, formatter or processor), its implementation language and the formats it covers. Installed tools come first, then tools written in Rust or Go. The last lines count the available tools.

docs.title: install
docs.text:
vfor install
vfor install --verbose

Install Homebrew, Node.js and a fixed set of tools, then write dprint.json, biome.json, ruff.toml and .vfor.json into the current directory if they are missing. The full list of actions is in Installation.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
vfor update
vfor update --verbose

Update Homebrew, npm and Rust, update the installed tools, clean the package manager caches, check each tool and refresh the plugin list in ./dprint.json. See Installation.

docs.title: configure
docs.text:
vfor configure init    # write an example .vfor.json in the current directory
vfor configure show    # print the effective settings and which config files exist
vfor configure         # print usage (action defaults to help)

init refuses to overwrite an existing .vfor.json. show lists max_workers, preferred_js_tool, preferred_css_tool, preferred_python_tool and create_backup, each with a source of default, environment or config file. The source column is a simple guess: it says config file whenever ./.vfor.json exists, even if that file does not set the value. See Configuration.

docs.title: ignore
docs.text:
vfor ignore init [path]   # write .vforignore with common patterns into path
vfor ignore show [path]   # list the patterns that apply in path
vfor ignore help          # print usage and pattern examples

action defaults to init and path to the current directory. init overwrites an existing .vforignore. show lists the first 20 patterns read from the ignore files described in Configuration.

docs.title: cleanup
docs.text:
vfor cleanup
vfor cleanup src/ --norecursive

Delete files ending in .vfor_backup or .vfor_temp below the path. Prints how many were removed, or No backup files found.

docs.title: benchmark
docs.text:
vfor benchmark src/
vfor benchmark src/ --operation=format --verbose
Argument Default Meaning path . Directory or file operation both minify, format or both verbose off Show more detail

The benchmark runs the operation in dry-run mode, so no file is changed and no tool is executed. It measures file discovery, validation and tool selection, and reports counts and timings per extension.

docs.title: perf_check
docs.text:
vfor perf_check src/ --create_baseline   # record a baseline
vfor perf_check src/                     # compare against it
Argument Default Meaning path . Directory to measure operation both minify, format or both create_baseline off Save a new baseline instead of comparing

Baselines are stored in ~/.cache/vfor/performance_baselines.json. A slow-down of more than 15 % against the baseline counts as a regression.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text:
vfor exits with 1 when it is interrupted with Ctrl+C and when an uncaught FileNotFoundError, PermissionError or other exception reaches the top level. An unknown command or bad argument makes Fire exit with 2.

Files that fail to process do not change the exit status, and neither does a path that does not exist: vfor fmt nonexistent --force prints nothing and exits with 0. Check the Failed: and Processed lines when you script around vfor.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
vfor reads settings from three places, in this order. A later source overrides an earlier one.

  1. Built-in defaults.
  2. JSON config files.
  3. Environment variables.

Flags on the command line apply to one run only.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Key Default Used for max_workers 4 Number of files processed in parallel by fmt, mini, benchmark exclude_patterns see below Patterns added to every run's exclusions preferred_js_tool esbuild Shown by vfor configure show; does not change tool choice in this version preferred_css_tool biome As above preferred_python_tool ruff As above preferred_html_tool html-minifier-terser Not shown, not used create_backup true Shown by vfor configure show; not used. The --backup flag decides, and it has no effect either; see Safety and backups

Default exclude_patterns:

[".git/**", "node_modules/**", ".venv/**", "venv/**", "__pycache__/**", "target/**",
 "dist/**", "build/**", "*.min.js", "*.min.css", "*.min.html", ".DS_Store", "Thumbs.db"]

docs.title: Config files
docs.text:
vfor looks for these files. When more than one exists, values from the higher one in this list win:

File Scope ./.vfor.json The directory you run vfor from ~/.vfor/config.json Your user account /etc/vfor/config.json The whole machine

A file must contain one JSON object. A file that is not valid JSON, or holds something other than an object, is ignored without a message.

exclude_patterns in a file replaces the default list rather than adding to it. Repeat the defaults you want to keep.

Create a starting point with:

vfor configure init

This writes ./.vfor.json:

{
    "preferred_js_tool": "esbuild",
    "preferred_css_tool": "biome",
    "preferred_python_tool": "ruff",
    "preferred_html_tool": "html-minifier-terser",
    "max_workers": 4,
    "create_backup": true,
    "exclude_patterns": [
        "*.min.*",
        "node_modules/**",
        "dist/**",
        "build/**",
        ".git/**"
    ]
}

Check what vfor sees with:

vfor configure show

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Setting Accepted values VFOR_MAX_WORKERS max_workers An integer VFOR_PREFERRED_JS_TOOL preferred_js_tool Any string VFOR_PREFERRED_CSS_TOOL preferred_css_tool Any string VFOR_PREFERRED_PYTHON_TOOL preferred_python_tool Any string VFOR_PREFERRED_HTML_TOOL preferred_html_tool Any string VFOR_CREATE_BACKUP create_backup true, 1, yes (anything else is false) VFOR_VERBOSE verbose Read into the settings but not used by any command

An invalid value, such as VFOR_MAX_WORKERS=many, is ignored.

VFOR_MAX_WORKERS=8 vfor fmt src/

docs.title: Exclusion patterns
docs.text:
For each run, the exclusion list is built from four parts:

  1. A fixed list in the file handler: the defaults above plus .next/**, .nuxt/**, coverage/**, *.backup, *.bak and *~.
  2. Patterns from the ignore files described below.
  3. exclude_patterns from the settings.
  4. The --exclude list from the command line.

Patterns use .gitignore syntax: *.log matches a file name anywhere, build/ or build/** a directory, and !keep.txt re-includes a file.

docs.title: Ignore files
docs.text:
vfor reads gitignore-style patterns from these files, relative to the directory being processed:

  1. <dir>/.gitignore
  2. <dir>/.vforignore
  3. <dir>/../.gitignore (the parent directory)
  4. ~/.vforignore_global

Blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped. All patterns from all four files are combined.

vfor ignore init <dir> writes a .vforignore with patterns for dependencies (node_modules/, .venv/, venv/, vendor/), build output (dist/, build/, *.min.js, *.min.css, *.min.html), temporary files (*.tmp, *.temp, *.log, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db), backup files (*.vfor_backup, *.vfor_temp) and editor files (.vscode/, .idea/, *.swp, *~). vfor ignore show <dir> prints the first 20 patterns found.

docs.title: Files vfor writes outside your project
docs.text: Path Written by Content ~/.cache/vfor/tool_cache.json every command Which tools are installed, valid for one hour ~/.cache/vfor/performance_baselines.json perf_check Performance baselines

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text: Path Content src/vexy_formi/cli.py The VFor class behind vfor src/vexy_formi/core.py FileProcessor, batch processing, results src/vexy_formi/tools.py ToolManager: tool lists, detection, execution src/vexy_formi/files.py FileHandler: file discovery, exclusions, validation src/vexy_formi/config.py Settings from defaults, JSON files and environment src/vexy_formi/safety.py Risk rating and the confirmation prompt src/vexy_formi/performance.py Baselines for perf_check src/vexy_formi/tools_install.py, tools_update.py vfor install and vfor update tests/ pytest suite; tests/fixtures/ holds one sample file per type testdata/ Larger JSON samples (about 11 MB), not shipped in the package src_docs/ Documentation source (this site) docs/ The built site, served by GitHub Pages

docs.title: Set up an environment
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-formi.git
cd vexy-formi
uv venv
uv pip install -e ".[dev,test]"

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
uv run python -m pytest -q -o addopts="" -n auto

The tests copy the fixtures into temporary directories before processing them, so the repository is not modified. Some tests depend on which external tools are installed. On a machine with biome, dprint, ruff, yq, black and jq but no esbuild, two tests failed (test_format_support, test_vfor_tools) and 72 passed.

docs.title: Lint and format
docs.text:
uvx ruff check src tests
uvx ruff format --respect-gitignore src tests

The pre-commit configuration runs Ruff and a set of whitespace and file checks.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: The version comes from git tags (vX.Y.Z) through hatch-vcs. At build time it is written to src/vexy_formi/__version__.py, which is not tracked in git. Between tags it looks like 1.0.5.dev0+gf3cc63237. Without a build, vexy_formi.__version__ falls back to the installed distribution's metadata, then to 0.0.0.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
./build.sh            # docs and package
./build.sh docs       # src_docs/ → docs/
./build.sh package    # dist/*.whl and dist/*.tar.gz, checked with twine

The source distribution contains the package, tests/, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE and pyproject.toml. The wheel contains the package only.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Sources are in src_docs/md/, the configuration in src_docs/mkdocs.yml. The site is built with ProperDocs and the MaterialX theme.

src_docs/build.sh          # strict build into docs/
src_docs/build.sh serve    # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000

The Docs workflow rebuilds docs/ on each push to main that touches src_docs/.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
1. Export a PyPI token for uv publish, for example UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN.

  2. Run:

    ./publish.sh

    gitnextver commits pending changes, tags the next vX.Y.Z and pushes. The script then builds from that tag and uploads with uv publish.

The pushed tag also triggers the Release workflow, which builds the package, uploads it to PyPI with skip-existing (so the upload from publish.sh does not make it fail) and creates a GitHub release.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: vexy-formi has two parts: the Python package that provides vfor, and the external formatters and minifiers it runs. You need both.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.10 or newer.
  • At least one external tool for each file type you want to process. See Tools and file types.

The Python dependencies are fire, rich, pathspec and chardet; the installer pulls them in.

docs.title: Install the package
docs.text:
uvpip 
uv tool install vexy-formi

python -m pip install vexy-formi

Check that the command is on your PATH:

vfor tools

The result is a table of 13 tools with ✓ Available or ✗ Missing next to each, followed by a line such as 6/13 tools available.

docs.title: Install the external tools
docs.text: You can install the tools yourself with your usual package manager, or let vfor install do it.

docs.title: Option 1: install only what you need
docs.text:
Pick tools from Tools and file types. For example, to format Python and JSON:

brew install ruff jq

Run vfor tools again; the new tools show as available. vfor caches the result of its tool check for one hour in ~/.cache/vfor/tool_cache.json. The cache is discarded early when PATH, HOME, VIRTUAL_ENV or NODE_PATH changes.

docs.title: Option 2: vfor install
docs.text:
vfor install installs a fixed set of tools. Read what it does before you run it; it changes your system and writes files into the current directory.

  1. If Homebrew is missing on macOS or Linux, it runs the official Homebrew install script.
  2. If npm is missing, it installs Node.js with Homebrew.
  3. With Homebrew it installs dprint, biome, esbuild, ruff, jq, yq and taplo.
  4. With npm install -g it installs @swc/cli and @swc/core, terser, lightningcss-cli, prettier and html-minifier-terser.
  5. With cargo it installs minhtml, and with Homebrew minify.
  6. In the current directory it creates dprint.json, biome.json, ruff.toml and .vfor.json, each only if the file does not exist yet.
  7. It prints a summary table.
cd ~/my-project     # the config files land here
vfor install --verbose

docs.title: Updating the tools
docs.text: vfor update runs brew update, npm update -g npm and rustup update, updates the tools it finds, cleans the package manager caches (brew cleanup, npm cache clean --force, cargo cache --autoclean) and checks each tool. If dprint.json exists in the current directory, it copies it to dprint.json.backup.<timestamp> and replaces its plugins list with pinned plugin versions.

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-formi.git
cd vexy-formi
uv pip install -e ".[dev,test]"

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
uvpip 
uv tool uninstall vexy-formi

python -m pip uninstall vexy-formi

This removes vfor only. Tools installed by vfor install stay; remove them with Homebrew, npm or cargo. Remove ~/.cache/vfor/ to delete the tool cache and performance baselines.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text: The package vexy_formi exposes the same machinery vfor uses. The calls on this page do not ask for confirmation, whatever the number of files; use dry_run=True while you try them out.

docs.title: Quick calls
docs.text:
import vexy_formi

result = vexy_formi.format("src/", dry_run=True)
print(result)

{'success': True, 'total_files': 7, 'successful': 7, 'failed': 0, 'total_time': 0.068…, 'errors': []}

vexy_formi.format(path, **kwargs) and vexy_formi.minify(path, **kwargs) are thin wrappers around format_files() and minify_files(). path is a string, a Path or a list of either.

Keyword arguments are passed to FileProcessor.format_files() or FileProcessor.minify_files():

Keyword Default Meaning recursive True Descend into subdirectories exclude_patterns None Extra gitignore-style patterns max_workers 4 Parallel workers create_backup True Accepted, but no backup is written; see Safety and backups dry_run False Pick tools but run none progress_callback None Called after each file; see below

Note

The keyword is exclude_patterns, not exclude. vexy_formi.format("src/", exclude=[...]) raises TypeError: FileProcessor.format_files() got an unexpected keyword argument 'exclude'.

The return value is a dictionary:

Key Meaning success True if at least one file succeeded total_files Files found successful, failed Counts total_time Seconds errors Error messages of the failed files size_reduction_bytes, size_reduction_percent Only from minify

docs.title: FileProcessor
docs.text:
For full results, use the class directly.

from pathlib import Path

from vexy_formi import FileProcessor

processor = FileProcessor()
result = processor.format_files(Path("src"), exclude_patterns=["*.py"], dry_run=True)
print(result.total_files, result.successful, result.success_rate)

for r in result.results:
    print(r.path.name, r.success, r.tool_used, r.error_message)

FileProcessor(config=None) loads the configuration when config is None.

Method Returns format_files(paths, recursive=True, exclude_patterns=None, max_workers=4, create_backup=True, dry_run=False, progress_callback=None) BatchResult minify_files(...) BatchResult, same arguments format_file(file_path, create_backup=True, dry_run=False) ProcessResult minify_file(file_path, create_backup=True, dry_run=False) ProcessResult

BatchResult fields: total_files, successful, failed, total_time, total_size_before, total_size_after, results (a list of ProcessResult). Properties: success_rate, total_size_reduction, total_size_reduction_percent.

ProcessResult fields: path, success, original_size, final_size, tool_used, processing_time, error_message. Properties: size_reduction_percent, size_change. In a dry run, tool_used ends in (dry-run).

docs.title: Progress callback
docs.text:
The callback is called from the main thread after each file finishes:

def on_progress(result, completed, total):
    print(f"{completed}/{total} {result.path.name}: {'ok' if result.success else result.error_message}")

processor.minify_files(Path("site"), progress_callback=on_progress, dry_run=True)

docs.title: Helpers
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path

from vexy_formi import detect_file_type, find_files, get_available_tools, validate_file

detect_file_type(Path("a.py"))          # 'python'
detect_file_type(Path("a.xyz"))         # None
validate_file(Path("src/app.py"))       # (True, None) or (False, "reason")
find_files(Path("src"), {".py", ".js"}) # list of Path, after exclusions and ignore files
get_available_tools()                   # names of tools found so far, e.g. ['ruff', 'biome', 'black']
  • detect_file_type() and validate_file() take a Path, not a string.
  • find_files(directory, extensions, exclude_patterns=None, recursive=True, respect_gitignore=True) applies the same exclusions and ignore files as vfor.
  • get_available_tools() lists only tools that have been checked so far. Tools are checked lazily (see Tools and file types), so the list can be shorter than what vfor tools shows.

docs.title: ToolManager
docs.text:
ToolManager(config=None) holds the tool lists and runs the tools.

from pathlib import Path

from vexy_formi import ToolManager

tm = ToolManager()
tm.is_available("ruff")                       # True or False
tm.get_format_command(Path("a.py"))           # ('ruff', ['ruff', 'format', '{input}'])
tm.get_minify_command_with_fallback(Path("a.js"))  # all installed minifiers for .js, in order
tm.supports_minify(Path("a.py"))              # False

tm.minify_commands and tm.format_commands are the dictionaries described in Tools and file types.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This page formats a small project, previews a minification, and then minifies. It follows the seven sample files that ship in the repository under tests/fixtures/: test.css, test.html, test.js, test.json, test.md, test.py and test.toml.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• vfor is installed. See Installation.
  • The project is under version control and committed, or you work on a copy. vfor rewrites files in place and, in this version, does not keep backups; see Safety and backups.

docs.title: 1. Make a test project
docs.text:
Copy the sample files into a scratch directory called proj:

git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-formi.git
mkdir proj
cp vexy-formi/tests/fixtures/* proj/

docs.title: 2. See which tools you have
docs.text:
vfor tools

On the machine used for this page, six of the 13 tools were available:

│ biome   │ ✓ Available │ Formatter │ Rust   │ JS, TS, JSON, CSS │
│ dprint  │ ✓ Available │ Formatter │ Rust   │ Multiple          │
│ ruff    │ ✓ Available │ Formatter │ Rust   │ Python            │
│ yq      │ ✓ Available │ Processor │ Go     │ YAML              │
│ black   │ ✓ Available │ Formatter │ Python │ Python            │
│ jq      │ ✓ Available │ Processor │ C      │ JSON              │
│ esbuild │ ✗ Missing   │ Minifier  │ Go     │ JS, TS            │
...
6/13 tools available
4 fast tools (Rust/Go) available

Which files vfor can process depends on this list. Tools and file types shows which tool handles which extension.

docs.title: 3. Preview the formatting
docs.text:
--dry_run finds the files and picks a tool for each, but runs nothing and changes nothing.

vfor fmt proj --dry_run --verbose

Processed 7 files  (preview)

In a dry run, the sizes shown are estimates from fixed ratios, not real results.

docs.title: 4. Format
docs.text:
vfor fmt proj --verbose

vfor runs the tools in parallel, four files at a time by default. In this run four files succeeded and three failed. The TOML file, for example, failed because taplo was missing and dprint found no dprint.json:

  test.toml: All format tools failed - dprint: dprint: No config file found at …/dprint.json. …

Successful files:
  test.json (0.116s)
  test.js (0.122s)
  test.css (0.024s)
  test.py (0.149s)

The number after each file is how long its tool took.

docs.title: 5. Preview a minification
docs.text:
vfor mini proj --dry_run --verbose

Failed files:
  test.html: No minification tool available for .html
  test.js: No minification tool available for .js

Successful files:
  test.json (617 → 493 bytes, +20.1%)
  test.css (608 → 425 bytes, +30.1%)

Without esbuild, swc or terser, JavaScript cannot be minified; without html-minifier-terser, HTML cannot either. Python, Markdown and TOML are never minified.

A positive percentage is a size reduction.

docs.title: 6. Minify
docs.text:
vfor mini proj --verbose

  ✓ test.json (+20.6%)
  ✓ test.css (+9.2%)

Failed: 2 files
Processed 2 files, +6.0% size (0.12s)

test.json is now on one line, compacted by jq -c. test.css was rewritten by biome format --write, the fallback when lightningcss is missing; that is formatting, not true minification, which is why it shrank by only 9.2%.

docs.title: 7. Exclude files
docs.text:
Pass extra exclusion patterns to --exclude as a list:

vfor fmt proj --exclude='["*.py", "legacy/**"]'

Warning

Give --exclude a list in square brackets. A bare string such as --exclude "*.py" is split into single characters, one of which is *, and every file is excluded.

For patterns you use every time, create a .vforignore file:

vfor ignore init proj

docs.title: 8. Large runs
docs.text:
When a run touches 100 files or more, 50 MB or more in total, or a single file of 50 MB or more, vfor prints a summary and asks Do you want to continue? [y/N]. Answer y to go on. Add --force to skip the question, for example in scripts.

vfor fmt src/ --force

docs.title: Safety and backups
docs.text: vfor fmt and vfor mini rewrite your files in place. This page describes what vfor checks before it touches a file, when it asks for confirmation, and what it does not do.

docs.title: Use version control
docs.text:
The most reliable undo is git. Commit or stash before a run, then review the result:

git stash            # or: git commit -am "before vfor"
vfor fmt src/
git diff --stat

If you do not like the result, git checkout -- src/ restores the files.

docs.title: Backups are not written in this version
docs.text:
The README, the --backup flag (on by default) and the create_backup setting all describe backup files. In version 1.0.x, none are written:

  • fmt and mini hand each file to the external tool, which writes its output straight over the original. That code path receives the backup setting but does not use it.
  • A test run of vfor mini and vfor fmt on the sample files left no *.vfor_backup file behind, and vfor cleanup reported No backup files found.

The library does contain an atomic-write helper (FileHandler.atomic_write) that copies the original to <name>.vfor_backup, writes to a temporary file and renames it, but fmt and mini do not call it. vfor cleanup exists to remove .vfor_backup and .vfor_temp files left by such writes.

docs.title: What is skipped
docs.text:
Before a file is processed it must pass these checks. A file that fails one is reported as failed, with the reason, and left unchanged.

Check Failure message starts with The path exists and is a regular file File does not exist / Path is not a file Size is not zero and not over 100 MB Empty file / File too large Readable and writable by you a permission diagnosis Not binary: no known binary extension (.png, .pdf, .zip, .svg, .exe, …) and content that looks like text Binary file detected Can be opened for appending, so it is not locked File is locked or permission denied Its encoding can be detected and decoded an encoding message A tool exists for its extension No minification tool available for .<ext> / No formatting tool available for .<ext>

When you give a directory, files are also filtered by extension and by the exclusion patterns described in Configuration, before any of these checks.

docs.title: When vfor asks for confirmation
docs.text:
Before a real run (not --dry_run), unless you pass --force, vfor collects the list of files and rates the run:

Condition Risk 1000 files or more critical 500 MB or more in total critical Any single file of 50 MB or more critical 100 files or more high 50 MB or more in total high Anything else low

For a high or critical run, vfor prints the summary, any warnings (for example that the path is inside a git repository), recommendations and the risk level, then asks:

Do you want to continue? [y/N]:

Anything other than y or yes cancels the run with Operation cancelled. Ctrl+C also cancels it.

In scripts, use --force to skip the question, or --dry_run to check first.

docs.title: Dry runs
docs.text: --dry_run goes through file discovery, validation and tool selection, then stops. It does not start any tool. The sizes it reports are estimates from fixed ratios, for example 65 % of the original for .js when minifying and 110 % for .json when formatting. Use it to see which files would be touched and which tool each would get, not to predict the result.

docs.title: Parallel processing
docs.text: Files are processed by a pool of max_workers threads (four by default). Each file is handled by one tool at a time, so a file is never written by two tools at once. The order in which files finish, and in which --verbose lists them, is not fixed.

docs.title: Tools and file types
docs.text: vfor does not format or minify anything itself. For every file it looks up the extension in a fixed, ordered list of external tools and runs the first one that is installed. The lists are defined in ToolManager._setup_tool_commands() in src/vexy_formi/tools.py.

docs.title: How a tool is chosen
docs.text:
1. Take the file's extension in lower case, for example .js.
  2. Walk the list for that extension and operation from top to bottom.
  3. Skip tools that are not installed. A tool counts as installed when which <tool> (where on Windows) finds it, or when <tool> --version exits with 0.
  4. Run the first installed tool on the file.
  5. If it fails, run the next installed tool in the list. If every tool fails, the file fails with All <operation> tools failed - followed by each tool's error.

A tool that exits with an error whose message suggests a temporary problem (for example resource temporarily unavailable or device busy) is retried up to two more times. Each tool run has a 30-second time limit.

The order is fixed. The preferred_*_tool settings in Configuration are read but do not change it in this version.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
vfor fmt handles these extensions. {file} is the file being processed; every command rewrites it in place.

Extension Tools, in order of preference Command .py ruff, black ruff format {file} · black {file} .js, .ts biome, prettier, dprint biome format --write {file} · prettier --write {file} · dprint fmt {file} .jsx, .tsx biome, prettier as above .css, .scss biome, prettier as above .html prettier, biome as above .json biome, prettier, jq as above · jq . {file} .toml taplo, dprint taplo fmt {file} · dprint fmt {file} .yaml, .yml prettier, yq prettier --write {file} · yq -i e . {file} .md dprint, prettier dprint fmt {file} · prettier --write {file}

.htm and .jsonc are not formatted.

docs.title: Minify
docs.text:
vfor mini handles these extensions.

Extension Tools, in order of preference Command .js esbuild, swc, terser esbuild {file} --minify --outfile={file} · swc {file} --minify -o {file} · terser {file} -c -m -o {file} .ts, .jsx, .tsx esbuild, swc as above .css lightningcss, biome lightningcss {file} -o {file} --minify · biome format {file} --write .scss lightningcss as above .html, .htm html-minifier-terser html-minifier-terser {file} -o {file} --collapse-whitespace --remove-comments .json jq jq -c . {file}, output written back to the file .jsonc biome biome format {file} --write

Two entries are not real minifiers. For .css without lightningcss, and for .jsonc, the tool is biome format, which reformats the file and may make it larger.

Python, Markdown, TOML and YAML files are never minified.

docs.title: The tool list in vfor tools
docs.text: Tool Type Written in Formats esbuild minifier Go JS, TS swc minifier Rust JS, TS biome formatter Rust JS, TS, JSON, CSS ruff formatter Rust Python lightningcss minifier Rust CSS taplo formatter Rust TOML dprint formatter Rust Multiple terser minifier Node.js JS prettier formatter Node.js Multiple black formatter Python Python jq processor C JSON yq processor Go YAML html-minifier-terser minifier Node.js HTML

docs.title: Tool settings
docs.text:
vfor passes no settings of its own to the tools; the commands above are run exactly as shown, from the directory where you started vfor. Each tool finds and reads its own configuration files the way it normally does.

dprint refuses to run without a configuration file. vfor install writes a starter dprint.json into the current directory; you can also run dprint init.

docs.title: The tool cache
docs.text:
Each tool check starts a subprocess, so vfor caches the results in ~/.cache/vfor/tool_cache.json:

  • The cache is valid for one hour.
  • It is discarded early when PATH, HOME, VIRTUAL_ENV or NODE_PATH changes.
  • On a cache miss, only ruff, biome, prettier, black and esbuild are checked at once; other tools are checked the first time a file needs them.
  • If a tool disappears between the check and the run, it is marked unavailable in the cache.

Delete the file to force a fresh check.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Start with:

vfor tools              # which tools are installed?
vfor configure show     # which settings are in effect?
vfor fmt src/ --dry_run --verbose   # which files would be touched, with which tool?

docs.title: vfor fmt prints nothing at all
docs.text:
No files were found. Check:

  • The path exists. vfor does not report a missing path; it just finds no files.
  • The files have an extension vfor handles for that operation. See Tools and file types.
  • The files are not excluded. node_modules/, dist/, build/, .venv/, *.min.js and similar are excluded by default, and so is everything listed in .gitignore, .vforignore, the parent directory's .gitignore and ~/.vforignore_global. vfor ignore show <dir> lists the ignore-file patterns.
  • You did not pass --exclude as a plain string. See the next section.

docs.title: Every file is excluded after --exclude "*.py"
docs.text:
--exclude expects a list. A plain string is split into single characters, and the character * matches everything. Write the list in brackets:

vfor fmt src/ --exclude='["*.py"]'

docs.title: No formatting tool available for .<ext> or No minification tool available for .<ext>
docs.text: None of the tools for that extension is installed, or the extension is not supported for that operation at all (for example, .py with mini). Install one of the tools listed in Tools and file types and run vfor tools to confirm. If a tool you just installed still shows as missing, delete ~/.cache/vfor/tool_cache.json.

docs.title: All format tools failed - dprint: … No config file found
docs.text: dprint needs a dprint.json. Run dprint init in the project, or let vfor install write a starter file. Alternatively install a tool that comes earlier in the list for that extension (for TOML, taplo).

docs.title: <tool> timed out after 30 seconds
docs.text: Each tool run is limited to 30 seconds. Very large files can hit this. Process them separately or with the tool directly.

docs.title: Binary file detected, Empty file, File too large
docs.text: The file failed a pre-check and was left unchanged. See Safety and backups for the list.

docs.title: File is locked or permission denied
docs.text: vfor could not open the file for writing. Check the file's permissions and whether another program holds it open.

docs.title: A CSS file got bigger after vfor mini
docs.text: Without lightningcss, CSS "minification" falls back to biome format --write, which formats rather than minifies. Install lightningcss (npm install -g lightningcss-cli) and run again.

docs.title: My preferred_js_tool setting is ignored
docs.text: In this version the preferred_*_tool settings are read and shown by vfor configure show, but tool choice always follows the fixed order in Tools and file types. To use a different tool, uninstall the ones before it in the list, or call the tool directly.

docs.title: No .vfor_backup files were created
docs.text: That is the current behaviour; see Safety and backups. Use version control to undo changes.

docs.title: vfor stopped and asked Do you want to continue? [y/N]
docs.text: The run touches 100 files or more, 50 MB or more, or a file of 50 MB or more. Answer y, or pass --force.

docs.title: --help after a command runs the command
docs.text:
Fire passes --help on to the command. Put -- before it:

vfor mini -- --help

docs.title: --no-backup is not recognised
docs.text: Fire's syntax for turning off a flag is --no followed by the flag name with no hyphen: --nobackup, --norecursive.

docs.title: TypeError: … unexpected keyword argument 'exclude' in Python
docs.text: The Python keyword is exclude_patterns. See Python API.
